newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank to delay debenture float.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank to delay debenture float.

text.p: Bangkok Bank Plc said on Thursday it would delay floating its planned long-term foreign bonds and debentures due to negative market sentiment on the sliding Thai economy and perceived uncertainty over government economic policies.

Senior Bangkok Bank executive Piyapan Chayanithi told reporters the decision to put off the planned bond issues could be attributed to Thailand's unfavourable economic outlook which would raise the cost for the bank to fund its new foreign loans.

Thailand economy is in a sharp downturn and official forecasts for economic growth of 5.9 percent for 1997 against 6.4 percent posted in 1996 is the worst expected in over a decade. The baht in mid-May came under speculative attack and the central bank has responded to offshore speculators by cutting off baht supply to them from local sources.
Bangkok Bank said in March that it planned to float $1.5 billion of subordinated perpetual bonds of 30-100 years and another $1.5 billion of 30-year debentures under its medium term note programme.
Piyapan said his bank could delay the bond issues as it does not require to mobilise new funds for refinancing its debts. He said the current sluggish Thai economy has slowed its lending growth.
Bangkok bank is the third Thai financial institution to delay floating of bonds this week. They have all blamed similar negative market conditions for their delay in flotations.
The others to delay their planned floats are the Siam Commercial bank Plc and the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand.
